mission.name: IM-1 Odysseus (Intuitive Machines, CLPS)
mission.tli_note: Falcon 9 second-stage burn ended at T+00:42:33 (launch timeline); the stage put Odysseus on its translunar path.
mission.loi_note: 408 s LOI burn reported complete at 09:20 CST (15:20 UTC); periselene taken at mid-burn.
mission.surface_end_note: Lander powered down on 29 February at the onset of local night (date only). It landed tipped over, so its panels saw less Sun than an upright lander would.
mission.orbit_note: 92 km circular lunar orbit (reported). Inclination not published; polar assumed.
launch_windows: Original multi-day window opening 12 January (Intuitive Machines, 27 Oct 2023); the launch slipped to the next month's window when SpaceX rescheduled.
Three-day window, 14 February primary, 15 and 16 backup (SpaceX, 5 Feb 2024). Launched 15 February.

mission.name: IM-2 Athena (Intuitive Machines, CLPS)
mission.tli_note: Athena was deployed about 45 minutes after launch, already on its translunar path; TLI taken a few minutes earlier (±10 min).
mission.loi_note: 492 s LOI burn reported complete at 06:27 CST (12:27 UTC); periselene taken at mid-burn.
mission.surface_end_note: Last contact 7 March: the lander came to rest on its side in a crater and its batteries ran down. This end is not a lighting limit.
mission.orbit_note: Circular orbit with a ~2 h period (reported), about 100-120 km; 100 km polar assumed.
launch_windows: Four-day window opening no earlier than 26 February (Intuitive Machines). Launched 27 February.

mission.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Firefly Aerospace, CLPS)
mission.tli_note: Firefly reported the TLI burn on 8 February 2025 without a time (after 25 days in Earth orbit); noon UTC assumed, +-12 h. It only sets the transit time of the reconstructed transfer; the landing analysis starts from the LOI below.
mission.loi_note: 4 min 15 s LOI burn starting 7:51 pm CST on 13 February (01:51 UTC on 14 February); periselene taken at mid-burn.
mission.surface_end_note: Final data around 6:15 pm CDT on 16 March, just over 5 hours into the lunar night: the solar-powered lander ran its batteries down after sunset, as planned. More than 14 days on the surface, 346 hours of daylight.
mission.orbit_note: Elliptical capture orbit, lowered to ~120 km on 18 February and to a near-circular orbit with a 100 km perilune on 24 February (Firefly). 100 km circular assumed. Inclination not published: 22-158 deg tried.
sources: Firefly live updates: burns, orbit, landing, end of mission
LOI and 16 days of checkout in lunar orbit
mission.wait_note: Firefly planned 16 days in lunar orbit for checkout before descent (announced at LOI, 16 February). The browser may wait up to 20 days, enough not to cut its search; its rule still takes the earliest feasible option, so the limit does not choose the day.
mission.scan_note: Blue Ghost spent 25 days in Earth orbit between launch and TLI, so its launch day was not tied to the Moon's position and there is no launch window to predict. The TLI-day scan is shown for reference only.
mission.sunset_note: Derived: 346 hours of daylight after the 08:34 UTC touchdown (Firefly, 17 March) put sunset at 18:34 UTC; the last data, 'just over 5 hours into the lunar night' at about 23:15 UTC, put it shortly before 18:15. Taken as 18:30 UTC, +-20 min. Pass if the browser's flat-horizon sunset is within 3 h (fixed before the first run: 1 deg of unmodelled horizon moves sunset by ~2 h at this latitude).
